properties.description: Pride & Prejudice (2005), directed by Joe Wright and starring Keira Knightley, Matthew Macfadyen, and Brenda Blethyn, is a romantic period drama adapted from the classic novel. Set in late 18th-century English society, it follows a sharp-witted young woman whose initial dislike of a proud gentleman gradually gives way to understanding and love. The film foregrounds character-driven emotion, social manners, and questions of class and marriage, rendered in a lyrical, naturalistic visual style. Its tone is intimate and heartfelt, balancing wit with wistful romantic longing.

properties.description: Pride and Prejudice (1940), directed by Robert Z. Leonard and starring Greer Garson, Laurence Olivier, and Mary Boland, is a studio-era comedy-drama romance adapted from the classic novel. Produced in black-and-white and presented by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, the film turns Jane Austen's tale of courtship and class into a witty, broadly comic costume picture. It foregrounds social satire, family dynamics, and romantic misunderstandings while emphasizing elegant production design and theatrical performances.

short_descriptions.value: When wealthy bachelors arrive in a small English town, families with marriageable daughters—notably the Bennets—compete for advantageous matches, sparking social maneuvering and romantic entanglements.

Als wohlhabende Junggesellen in einer englischen Kleinstadt eintreffen, wetteifern Familien mit heiratsfähigen Töchtern—insbesondere die Bennets—um gute Partien, was zu sozialen Verwicklungen und Liebesgeschichten führt.

La llegada de solteros adinerados a un pueblo inglés provoca que familias con hijas en edad de casarse—especialmente los Bennet—compitan por buenos matrimonios, desatando enredos sociales y románticos.

L'arrivée de célibataires fortunés dans un village anglais pousse des familles avec filles en âge de se marier—surtout les Bennet—à rivaliser pour de bons partis, déclenchant intrigues sociales et amoureuses.

properties.description: Pride and Prejudice (2003), directed by Andrew Black and starring Kam Heskin, Orlando Seale, and Lucila Solá, is a contemporary comedic romance that transposes Jane Austen's courtship tale to modern‑day Utah. The film follows an aspiring writer in college who prioritizes her career while repeatedly clashing with a proud businessman, translating themes of pride, misunderstanding, and social expectation into modern dating rituals. With a hip, art-directed look and an indie sensibility, it emphasizes witty dialogue, family pressure, and the emotional work of reconciliation. The overall tone is warm and humorous, offering a fresh, youthful spin on a classic story.

properties.description: Pride and Prejudice and Zombies (2016), directed by Burr Steers and starring Lily James, Sam Riley and Jack Huston, is a genre-mashing adaptation that blends action, comedy, fantasy, horror and romance. Set in early 19th-century England, it follows five sisters trained as warriors who must balance courtship and social expectation while combating a spreading zombie plague. The film preserves Austen-like dialogue and social satire while layering in frequent zombie set pieces and choreographed combat, exploring themes of marriage, gender roles, duty and survival. Tonally it mixes witty period romance with visceral, often comic horror to create an escapist, darkly playful experience.

properties.description: Pride and Prejudice: A New Musical (released 2020, directed by Robert Kelley) is a musical film adaptation of Jane Austen's novel starring Monique Hafen Adams, Samantha Jane Ayoob, and Seton Chiang. Presented as a stage-style screen musical, it preserves the original's social wit and courtship drama while adding new songs and interpretive moments to clarify characters' motivations. The production leans into romantic and nostalgic themes—class, pride, misunderstanding, and eventual reconciliation—delivered with warm, uplifting musical performances and theatrical staging.
